correctness.rationale: For every m>=2, reductions at infinitely many good q≡1(mod m) preserve the complex intersection lattice. A complete four-case finite-field count gives characteristic polynomial χ_m; exact Orlik–Solomon and product decomposition give projective Betti numbers. Its cubic discriminant equals a strictly negative polynomial in n=m-2, so Terao factorization forbids freeness. Checker exactly verified several finite fields and discriminant algebra; those checks are corroboration, not infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The original July 2026 family and numerical incidence counts do not include the exact uniform characteristic and projective Betti polynomials or uniform non-freeness. The 2009 general gain-graph chromatic subset expansion gives a method but not the closed K2,2 cyclic evaluation; the latter requires a nontrivial collapse of exponentially many subsets and an exact uniform discriminant analysis. Comparisons with 2024 bias arrangements and 2026 additive gain deformations concern different defining hyperplanes. Specializations implicit in older literature remain a residual risk.
residual_risks: The 2009 general gain-graph chromatic subset expansion algorithmically covers this family, though a directly evaluated exact formula and discriminant result were not located; a specialized old computation could subsume the proposed closed evaluation.
No independent audit has assessed the new computations or the full bibliographic landscape.

value.rationale: An infinite family motivated by the first non-skew refined-Purdy counterexample receives a complete closed characteristic polynomial and projective complement Betti numbers. Uniform non-freeness is a structural conclusion with a strict discriminant proof, not an arbitrary small finite sample; unlike general gain-graph counting methods, the formulas give directly usable information on this explicit family.
